newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 17.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet:
biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Pioneer
LEFT PARTY MAY SHOOT DOWN JUDGES' BILL

The government's move to push through a constitutional amendment bill to restore the primacy of the executive in the appointments and transfers of judges has run into rough weather. Even as official sources indicated the bill might be tabled in the lower house on Monday, the Communist Party (Marxist), a coalition partner, said it would oppose it. The Left parties are in favour of a judicial commission. The Left's stand largely coincides with that of the opposition Bharatiya Janata Party, which has reservations over constitutionally enforcing the executive's position.
The Economic Times
EURO EMISSION NORMS MAY PITCHFORK CAR EXPORTS

The government may adopt European norms for controlling gas and suspended particle emissions in exhaust from diesel vehicles. The Indian driving cycle may also be replaced with the European one. The norms would require automobile manufacturers to get their models approved and maintain conformity of production. European norms, called Euro One, were less strict than those in the United States but were easier to implement. They were also expected to help car exporters.
INFLATION AT 7.78 PCT

Due to a decline in the prices of edible items, the inflation rate receded for the second consecutive week ended March 1 by 0.13 percentage point to 7.78 percent. It continued its longest spell of staying at a single digit level. Inflation, based on the wholesale price index and on point-to-point basis, was 7.91 in the previous week.
MAJORS PREPARING FOR POLYMER PRICE HIKE

Domestic petrochemicals majors planned another price hike of polymers. After a tough 1996, the companies planned to improve their margins and ride the boom in the international markets likely to be triggered off by the drying up of ethylene in global markets and maintenance closure of some South Korean naphtha cracker units in April and May. With spot cargoes of ethylene difficult to fund with tight supplies across Asia, global traders received enquiries for prompt shipment to India, but no contracts were clinched.
HINDUSTAN LEVER CONTINUES TO HUG CHEMICALS BUSINESS

Hindustan Lever (HLL) will continue to develop its chemicals business even though parent Unilever decided to quit the business. The chief executive officer of Unilever NV said the chemicals business contributed substantially to the company's growth prospect and its future would be decided by the board of the Indian company. However, Unilever would have to make an arrangement with the buyer of its chemicals business to protect HLL's rights, he added.
GOVERNMENT TO NET 25 BILLION MORE FROM TAX

The Finance Ministry expects to collect about 25 billion rupees through the Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) by March-end. The positive trend in collections through MAT was reinforced, with Reliance Industries Ltd coughing up 500 million rupees as tax. Apart from many leading corporates, several profitable public sector companies, which enjoy the benefit of high depreciation from income tax, will also end up paying MAT. Through December 1996, there had been a shortfall of about 15 billion rupees as against the budgeted target set for excise collection alone.
Financial Express
ISPAT SET TO LAUNCH REWORKED RIGHTS ISSUE

Ispat Industries, the Mittal group flagship, reworked its plan of entering the domestic primary market with a eight billion rupee rights issue. The issue was likely to hit the market early in April. The proposed 2:1 issue, of fully convertible debentures, would partly finance the company's 47.92 billion rupee three million tonne hot roll mill plant coming up in Maharashtra. The plant would also have a blast furnace and a captive power unit. The first phase would kick off by end-1997 and the second by the next year.
MORE BANKS TO SEEK FORWARD COVER IN DOLLAR

More banks are likely to seek forward cover in dollars of a longer duration this week from the existing practice of two-day rollovers of foreign currency deposits, due to rising dollar premiums. Already some banks were seeking forward cover, bankers said. Premiums that were climbing ever since the apex bank stepped in about 10 days back were seen firming even further, they said. Banks, mainly foreign-owned with a large foreign currency deposit base, restricted their rollovers of their foreign currency deposit to a two-day swap since February because the low premium reduced costs and increased spreads on such deposits.
BHARTI TELECOM'S ARM TO BRING OUT ADR BY JUNE-END

After repeated postponements, Bharti Televentures' $125 million American Depository Receipts (ADR) issue was expected to be launched by June-end. The company was in the process of shortlisting lead managers to handle the issue. Bharti Televentures would be offloading about 20 percent of its equity in the ADR issue, sources said. Bharti Telecom, the holding company, holds 80 percent stake with STET of Italy holding the rest in the company. With the 20 percent offloading, the shareholding pattern of Bharti Telecom and STET would be diluted to 65 and 15 percent, respectively.
Business Standard
OUTLOOK FOR CORPORATES GRIM, BUT MDCS BEAT RECESSION

The results of 208 companies for six months through December 1996 showed a negative growth in net profit. The trend revealed that the recession and liquidity crunch were not over yet. Multinational companies were not affected although they may suffer a negative profit growth in the second half of the year. While net profit of September 1996 declined by over 10 percent, the net profit of these 208 companies declined by 16.8 percent. Their sales growth was modest at 13.5 percent while the cost of funds shot up by 43.2 percent.
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS MAY LIMIT DEBT EXPOSURE IN POWER

Financial institutions (FIs) are likely to limit their debt exposure in power projects to 50 percent of the total project cost. This followed their reluctance to bear the risk associated with such projects. At present, FIs can have a maximum debt exposure of 70 percent in power projects, of which, 40 percent accounted for disbursals in rupee terms and the rest on guaranteeing offshore debt. The new proposal limited total debt component to half the project cost, with FIs free to fix the break-up. For the remaining cost, a minimum of 25 percent would be brought in by the promoters and their associates with the balance coming in as debt or equity.
HOECHST'S INDIAN ARMS TO COME UNDER PARENTS' CONTROL

Hoechst AG of Germany is restructuring the shareholding pattern in its Indian subsidiary following its decision to transform itself into a holding company worldwide. The 50.1 percent holding of Hoechst AG in Hoechst Marion Roussel (HMR) India would be transferred to HMR Germany which would control the Indian subsidiary. This move would bring HMR India directly under its pharma parent in Germany and not under Hoechst AG. The transfer, in the offing for quite sometime, would now take place shortly.
MOVE TO SIMPLIFY DEPRECIATION RATES

The expert panel set up to recast the Companies Act, was prepared for a debate on a radical proposal to rationalise and simplify depreciation rates for industry. As a first step, it called for a public debate on the issue of prescribing a minimum rate of depreciation using the single line method. The proposal also provided for rounding off the existing rates and reducing the number of slabs. Presently, companies were free to choose either the single line method or the written down value method. Though the panel favoured continuing with both methods, the government was likely to seek a uniform method, if various industry sections agreed on rationalising the rates.
The Observer
FINANCE MINISTER DISCOUNTS DEBT CRISIS, MOODY'S RATING

The finance minister dismissed criticism from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the U.S. credit rating agency Moody's. Commenting on an IMF report that said India could face a debt crisis unless it made deeper cuts in the fiscal deficit, he said the IMF offered text-book advice. The minister said Moody's rating was wrong. Moody's did not take into account the budget, he added, referring to the tax and spending blueprint for fiscal 1997/98 (April- March). Meanwhile, bankers and corporates were watching the outcome of his proposed meeting with the apex bank's chief.
UK INVESTORS CAUTIOUS TO VSNL PITCH

British investors seemed cautious in their response to the roadshow by Videsh Sanchar Nigam (VSNL). Most investors seemed to have adopted a wait-and-watch position until the pricing of the issue was declared. The roadshow meeting threw up some contradictions inherent in the way Western investors see India. Most of the questions asked by prospective investors related to monopoly and the revenue sharing process.
NON-FOOD CREDIT REGISTERS SLOWER GROWTH

Notwithstanding the government's claims of the improving liquidity position, non-food credit registered a slower growth in the current fiscal as compared to the previous year. The central bank's statistics showed non-food credit disbursements by commercial banks increased by 146.02 billion rupees between April 1996 and February 14, 1997, as against an increase of 341.96 billion in 1995/96 (April-March). Opposed to this, the rate of growth of aggregate deposits of commercial banks was much higher in 1996/97 than in the previous year.
Business Line
PAKISTAN ALLOWS DRUG INPUT IMPORTS FROM INDIA

Pakistan decided to permit import of basic raw materials from India for its domestic pharmaceutical industry in an effort to make drugs cheaper in that country. Sources said the decision was taken because medicine prices were higher in Pakistan than those in neighbouring countries. Pakistan has been importing raw materials from countries except India and Israel.
